title: Does Inter-Model Homogeneity Predict Enterprise AI Pilot Failure?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Correlational survey design establishes association but not causation between portfolio homogeneity and failure. The link is plausible but has a causal gap: many confounders (org size, use case complexity) could explain the same correlation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires recruiting enterprise practitioners, designing a valid survey instrument, and obtaining organizational data. This is social science methodology that CS beginners lack training in. Access to enterprise contacts is a significant barrier.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Survey design, participant recruitment, data collection, and statistical analysis across organizations is an open-ended effort with unclear timelines. Not feasible in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Extensive enterprise AI failure literature exists but focuses on organizational, data, and process factors. No study has examined whether inter-model homogeneity in an organization's AI portfolio predicts pilot failure rates. The Deloitte finding about portfolio diversity improving returns is adjacent but does not measure model output homogeneity. This specific correlation is unstudied.

evidence.source: MIT report: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing (Fortune, 2025)
evidence.finding: 95% of AI pilot programs fail to achieve rapid revenue acceleration. Focuses on ROI and organizational factors, not model homogeneity.

evidence.source: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise (2026)
evidence.finding: Organizations building AI portfolios with diverse risk profiles report 3.7x to 10.3x returns. Touches on portfolio diversity but not model homogeneity specifically.
Identifies data quality, technical maturity, and skills as top obstacles. Does not analyze model portfolio homogeneity as a failure predictor.
